review: The hymn is the self-address of Ps 42–43: 1:1–8 is Ps 42:6 (מַה־תִּשְׁתּוֹחֲחִי נַפְשִׁי) with Ps 42:12 (יְשׁוּעֹת פָּנַי אֱלֹהָי), 2:1–8 is Ps 42:6 with Ps 65:3 and 1 John 4:8, 3:1–8 is Heb 9:15–22 with Heb 7:25 and 4:15, and 4:1–8 is Ps 30:6 (בָּעֶרֶב יָלִין בֶּכִי וְלַבֹּקֶר רִנָּה) with Rev 19:7.

The hymn's addressee is the soul, feminine throughout the Arabic; the Hebrew keeps the feminine forms (אָתְּ, אֲדֹנַיִךְ, בִּטְחִי, קַוִּי), because the psalm's self-address is grammatical and the gender is part of how the stanza speaks to itself.

1:6 כִּי טוֹב אֲדֹנָי לְעֵזֶר — the Arabic فَالرَّبُّ نِعْمَ الْمُعِين is 'the Lord is the best Helper'; the Hebrew uses the psalm's טוֹב with לְעֵזֶר (Ps 73:28, טוֹב־לִי קִרְבַת אֱלֹהִים), since a superlative 'best' would need a construction the short line cannot carry.

3:2 בְּדָם נֶחְקְקָה וְנִכְתְּבָה — the Arabic قَدْ سَطَّرَتْهُ الدِّمَاء is 'the bloods have inscribed it'; the Hebrew keeps the singular דָּם, as Gen 9:6 and Heb 9:22 do, and pairs חָקַק with כָּתַב, the engraving-and-writing pair of Isa 49:16 and Jer 31:33, so the covenant is a document written in blood.
